title: Averaged Extensions of Golomb's Triangular Recursion: Critical Invariance and Supercritical Constraints
summary: For an integer $m\ge 1$ and a parameter $α>0$, consider the nested recursion $$ Q_{α,m}(n)=1+\left\lfloor \fracα{m}\sum_{j=1}^m Q_{α,m}\!\left(n-Q_{α,m}(n-j)\right)\right\rfloor, \qquad n>m, $$ with $Q_{α,m}(1)=\cdots=Q_{α,m}(m)=1$. For $m=1$ and $α=1$, this is Golomb's non-homogeneous triangular recursion. We prove that its canonical triangular solution is preserved, up to an initial index shift, by every finite arithmetic averaging length.
